title: SYSK Selects: A Podcast on Zoot Suits? Yes
summary: SYSK Selects rerun, introduced by Josh, of the episode on zoot suits. The hosts open with odd local laws (including a Los Angeles ban on zoot suits) and a shout-out to listener Martin van Nostran's band. They trace the zoot suit's origins from the Harlem jazz and nightclub scene (with Cab Calloway's jive slang and the disputed Clyde Duncan/Gainesville, Georgia story), its adoption by Mexican American pachucos in Los Angeles as a symbol of identity and defiance, and its clash with wartime fabric rationing and the War Production Board's streamlined suit. They cover the Sleepy Lagoon murder case, the June 1943 clashes between sailors and pachucos in East Los Angeles, the Vengeance Squad, the Zoot Suit Riots that spread over several days, and the city ordinance banning zoot suits. They close with the zoot suit's legacy in juvenile delinquency films, a Mystery Science Theater 3000 clip from I Was a Teenage Werewolf, and listener mail on polygraphs and slang.

segments.title: Selects intro and band shout-out
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Selects episode on zoot suits. Hosts mention a T-shirt and CD from listener Martin van Nostran's band.

segments.title: Dumb laws
segments.summary: Chuck lists odd state and local laws, including the Los Angeles ban on wearing a zoot suit, which leads into the episode topic.

segments.title: What a zoot suit is
segments.summary: The hosts describe the zoot suit's broad padded shoulders, long coat, high-waisted pants, pegged ankles, watch chain, and hat, and compare it to later pimp fashion.

segments.title: Origins in Harlem and the jazz scene
segments.summary: Zoot suits spread through the Harlem Renaissance and nightclub scene. Malcolm X's zoot days are noted, Cab Calloway's jive slang defines the look, and origin stories are discussed, including the Clyde Duncan Gainesville, Georgia tale, which the hosts say is unproven.

segments.title: Pachucos and wartime rationing
segments.summary: In Los Angeles the zoot suit became a symbol of Mexican American identity and defiance. Wartime fabric rationing made the suit seem unpatriotic, and the War Production Board pushed a streamlined American suit.

segments.title: Racism, the press, and the Sleepy Lagoon case
segments.summary: Anti-Latino prejudice and press coverage linked zoot suiters to crime. The Sleepy Lagoon murder led to the railroading of young Mexican American defendants, later overturned on appeal.

segments.title: Zoot Suit Riots of 1943
segments.summary: Clashes between sailors and pachucos in East Los Angeles in June led to the Vengeance Squad's attacks and several days of mob violence by servicemen. The City Council banned zoot suits, and hundreds of Latinos were arrested.

segments.title: Legacy: juvenile delinquency films and 'I Was a Teenage Werewolf'
segments.summary: The hosts describe the zoot suit's legacy in juvenile delinquency and in 1950s films, and play a Mystery Science Theater 3000 clip from I Was a Teenage Werewolf.
